elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Subparagraph 18.8: "Teleglobe USA Inc. (the 'Customer') may terminate this Agreement as to the Customer, and its participation in this Agreement, for convenience at any time, whether during or after the Initial Period". There are no Order Forms in this consortium construction agreement, so termination of the Agreement as to Customer is the applicable form of the right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: 18.8: "by giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Parties" — exactly 30 days, written, and not conditioned on any consent or trigger. (The deterministic check 'Customer convenience termination present' returned false, but that is a mechanical regex miss: the phrase 'for convenience' is separated from the notice period by the interposed clause 'at any time, whether during or after the Initial Period'; the operative right is plainly present.)

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 18.8: "the other Parties shall refund to the Customer, pro rata, any charges prepaid by the Customer in respect of the period after the effective date of such termination." 'Pro rata' is expressly stated (not merely inferred from a post-termination period), and the payer is the counterparties.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained 18.1: "any Party may terminate its participation in this Agreement at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter by giving not less than one (1) year's prior notice" — the effective date is expressly anchored to the end of the 25-year Initial Period or later, so it is not a mid-term convenience right; 18.2 permits mid-term termination only "by agreement in writing of all the Parties", i.e. with Customer's own consent. No counterparty mid-term convenience exit exists, and 18.8 does not create one.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: 18.8 sets 30 days' notice, which is outside the 60–90 day band literally required by this fallback element (it is more favourable to us, but does not satisfy the stated range). Fallback level is therefore incomplete; preferred level is the operative target.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee or penalty attaches to an 18.8 exit. The only exit-side charge mechanic, the no-credit-for-capital-costs rule, is keyed solely to "a Party that terminates its participation in accordance with Subparagraph 18.1" and so does not bite on an 18.8 termination.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: 18.1 permits a Party's unilateral exit only "at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter"; the effective date is tied to term end, and mid-term termination under 18.2 requires unanimous written agreement.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 18.1 requires "not less than one (1) year's prior notice thereof, in writing, to the other Parties", exceeding 90 days.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: 18.8 supplies the Customer convenience right, the 30-day written notice, and an express pro-rata refund of prepaid charges, and retained 18.1/18.2 already deny the counterparties any mid-term convenience exit (18.1's effective date is expressly anchored to the end of the Initial Period, satisfying the term-end anchoring boundary).

The deterministic 'Customer convenience termination present' check is a false negative; inspected in substance, 18.8 contains an unconditional Customer election to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice, which is a convenience right under the rule boundaries. No repair is required on that basis.

Minimal: the insertion is purely additive ("In addition to Subparagraph 18.1"), 18.1, 18.2, the no-capital-credit sentence and 18.7 are retained verbatim, and no survival tail, at-own-expense language, procedure or other extra outside the preferred checklist is added. The clause was missing, so a concise insertion of wholly new words is acceptable.

Intent preserved: no defined term is left undefined, no cross-reference is left dangling, and no retained sentence contradicts 18.8. 18.4 and 18.7 remain keyed to 18.1, so the new exit simply sits outside them rather than conflicting with them.

Drafting notes (not defects at this level): (i) confirm from the signature block that Teleglobe USA Inc. is the party we represent before introducing "Customer" as a new defined term in a multi-party consortium agreement, and check that "Customer" is not used with a different meaning elsewhere; (ii) in a construction-consortium structure, verify that "charges prepaid by the Customer" captures the amounts we actually prepay (e.g. O&M or capacity charges) so the refund limb is not inoperative in practice; (iii) as flagged, expect the counterparties to seek extension of 18.7 (and possibly 18.4) to 18.8 — accepting 18.7 is tolerable, accepting 18.4 would import a no-capital-credit penalty on our convenience exit and should be resisted.
